Code to produce a heatmap using the ggplot2 function

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)

```


```{r}
getwd()
setwd("./phd/ppi/psicquicStringHippie-API")
getwd()
```

```{r}
# loading the big dataframe
df_final <- read.csv("interactors_of_VCAM1_HUMAN.csv")

# removing the first column (index from pandas)
df_interactors <- subset(df_final, select = -X)

```


```{r}
# Heatmap using the ggplot & geom_tile

# Formatting the data 
df_ggplot_string_escore <- select(df_interactors, 
                                          c("interactor_of_VCAM1_HUMAN", "string_escore")) %>% # selecting only the relevant columns # nolint
                                          replace(is.na(.), 0) %>% # replacing all the NA values with 0
                                          pivot_longer(cols="string_escore", names_to = "score") # pivoting to longer format needed for the heatmap # nolint

# Make the heatmap
ggplot(df_ggplot_string_escore,
       aes(interactor_of_VCAM1_HUMAN, score, fill = value))+
       geom_tile()

```

```{r}
# Formatting the data 
df_heatmap_string_escore <- select(df_interactors, c("interactor_of_VCAM1_HUMAN", "string_escore")) %>%
column_to_rownames(var ="interactor_of_VCAM1_HUMAN") %>%
replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
data.matrix()

# heatmap from the string e score
Heatmap(df_matrix_1, name = "string_escore",
    row_order = order(as.numeric(gsub("row", "", rownames(df_matrix_1)))), 
    column_order = order(as.numeric(gsub("column", "", colnames(df_matrix_1)))),
    column_title = "reorder matrix")
```
